quotes.text: Victory awaits him who has everything in order—luck, people call it. Defeat is certain for him who has neglected to take the necessary precautions in time; this is called bad luck.
quotes.original: Seier venter den, som har alt i orden — held kalder man det. Nederlag er en absolut følge for den, som har forsømt at ta de nødvendige forholdsregler i tide — uheld kaldes det.

translation.edition: The South Pole: An Account of the Norwegian Antarctic Expedition in the "Fram," 1910–1912, Vol. I (London: John Murray)

quotes.author: Roald Amundsen

source.work: Sydpolen: Den norske sydpolsfærd med Fram 1910–1912 (The South Pole)
source.locator: Norwegian: Bind 1, p. 506 (Kristiania: Jacob Dybwad, 1912); English: Chater tr., Vol. I, Chapter IX 'The End of the Winter'

quotes.verification_note: English matched verbatim in Chater's translation (Project Gutenberg #3414, Vol. I, Ch. IX; also in #4229). Norwegian original read from the National Library of Norway's OCR of the 1912 first edition, Bind 1 p. 506 (nb.no item ed55ef6f9348da975c792694c5591851); the OCR prints 'iorden', given here as 'i orden'.

quotes.text: I have always thought that the much-praised “line of retreat” is a snare for people who wish to reach their goal.
quotes.author: Fridtjof Nansen

source.work: Adventure (rectorial address, University of St Andrews, 3 November 1926), in Adventure, and Other Papers (London: Hogarth Press / L. & Virginia Woolf)

quotes.verification_note: Matched verbatim in the Internet Archive full text of the 1927 Hogarth Press edition (page header 26). Nansen delivered the address in English, so no translation is involved. The popular companion lines 'Never stop because you are afraid…' and 'The difficult is what takes a little time…' were NOT found in this text and are not used.

quotes.text: We took risks, we knew we took them; things have come out against us, and therefore we have no cause for complaint, but bow to the will of Providence, determined still to do our best to the last.

quotes.text: Courage is the price that Life exacts for granting peace.
quotes.author: Amelia Earhart

source.work: 20 Hrs. 40 Min.: Our Flight in the Friendship (New York: G. P. Putnam's Sons)
source.locator: Opening line of her poem 'Courage', printed in the book's front matter

quotes.verification_note: Matched in Project Gutenberg #73448 (front matter, before Chapter I). In the poem the line ends with a comma and continues; it is closed with a full stop here. The poem is Earhart's own (written 1927). Popular Earhart lines ('The most difficult thing is the decision to act…', 'The most effective way to do it, is to do it') were not found in this book and are not used.
